sentences.text:
Munavath Mothiya vs The Power Grid Corporation Of India Ltd
on 9 July, 2025
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Pulla Karthik
 Writ Petition No.18678 of 2025
Order:

entities.text: Munavath Mothiya vs The Power Grid Corporation Of India Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Aggrieved by the alleged action of respondent No.1 in entering and carrying out construction of 765 KV transmission line over the petitioners' land in Sy.No.285/A/E, Kadthal Village, without following due process of law, the present writ petition has been filed.

2. Heard Sri Pramod Maligi, learned counsel, representing Sri Safdar Mirza, learned counsel for the petitioners, Sri L. Ravichander, learned Senior Counsel, representing Sri Mayur Mundra, learned Standing Counsel for respondent No.1 and learned Government Pleader for Revenue, on behalf of respondent Nos.2 and 3.
With their consent, the Writ Petition is taken up for disposal at admission stage.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the petitioners are the absolute owners and possessors of the agricultural land situated in Sy.No.285/4/E, Kadthal Village and Mandal, Ranga Reddy District, having obtained the said land under the Government Welfare Schemes for Scheduled Tribes.

While so, during March, 2025, it was noticed that some labourers, along with heavy machinery and JCBs, were trespassing into the petitioners' subject land, and on inquiry, the PK, J petitioners were informed that respondent No.1 is constructing a 765 KV Transmission Line over the subject land.

However, it is contended that, no prior notice under Section 15 or 16 of the Indian Telegraph Act, 1885, or under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in the Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, (for short, 'the LAAR Act'), has been issued to the petitioners.

entities.text: Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Further, there has been no notice under Section 11(1) of the LAAR Act or any form acquisition proceedings initiated.

Therefore, learned counsel for the petitioners prays this Court to permit the petitioners to make a detailed representation to the respondents, ventilating their grievance, and seeks a direction to the respondents to consider the same and pass necessary orders within a reasonable period of time.
4. Learned Senior Counsel fairly submits that the respondents will consider the representation of the petitioners, as and when received, and pass appropriate orders in accordance with law.

5. Having regard to the submissions made by the learned counsel for the respective parties, without going into merits of the case, the Writ Petition is disposed of permitting the petitioners to make their representation to the respondents within a period of one (01) week PK, J from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
On receipt of such representation from the petitioners, the respondents shall consider the same and pass appropriate orders thereon, as expeditiously as possible, strictly in accordance with law.
Miscellaneous applications, if any, pending in this writ petition, shall stand closed.
